documentedDeviations.note: ETag clause only; the slot/header-shape clauses passed in round 1. The implementation's ETag has three segments ("<dayVersion>.<settingsVersion>.<flagBits>", e.g. "0.68.11"), not the contract's literal two - accepted in round 1, recorded only. After a hold plus a booking on a fresh date the version reaches 2 (the hold is itself a versioned write), not 1; the assertion clause itself holds.

The warmed Sites tab's plain reload issued a fresh fetch (no If-None-Match, no 304) in this browser session, so the user-visible check (closed note, zero stale chips, 200 with ETag "1.68.11") was complemented by two labelled mechanism proofs on the exact round-2 defect path: a curl replay of the pre-change ETag ("0.68.11") now returning 200 with the new body (round 2: 304 + stale body), and an in-page default-cache fetch returning the fresh online_closed payload. No cache bypass was substituted for the plain reload. On an online_closed day the operator availability answers 141 slots with dayState.state "online_closed" (staff channel unaffected) rather than 0 slots; 0 slots is the closed day's value, verified in step 3.
Carried forward from round 1 and accepted by the orchestrator; not re-opened in round 3 per the brief.

appliedUpdates.description: Added the "Round: guest-channels-and-crm user testing, ROUND 3" block before spawning validators: scope (VAL-CROSS-007 plus VAL-ONLINE-002's ETag clause only), the fix under test (commit d8b41f4e: readDayVersion 0 default, horizon-wide version bumps, max_parties in pacingWarning), the verified environment state (services 3007/3001/3008, all acme flags true, rate counters cleared, fresh dates 2026-11-29 and 2026-12-03 with dayVersion 0 / ETag "0.68.11"), the round-3 data-isolation registry (r3-etag-api: 2026-11-29; r3-cross007: 2026-12-03), the serial rule that the two groups must not overlap because pacing/service-availability writes bump every date's version, Flow Validator Guidance for agent-browser/curl/terminal (round 3), and the two-batch concurrency plan.

Added the round-3 results and runtime findings: both assertions pass; the parent-observed fix behaviour (first write moves dayVersion 0 -> 1; a hold is itself a versioned write so hold + booking ends at 2; the warmed browser did not revalidate so the mechanism proof is the curl replay plus a labelled default-cache fetch; operator online_closed returns the full slot list with dayState "online_closed"; operator availability now reports available:false / pacingWarning:true for a max_parties breach and the sheet shows the "*" marker and pacing alert; the sheet auto-ticks the pacing override; the replace-day operator read still lists all location services); and the round-3 leftover rows.

No correction needed: round 3 used the existing start/stop/healthcheck definitions for tenant-api-us (3007), app (3001, VITE_DIRECT_DEV=1) and sites (3008) as written; KSA (3009) and Admin (3005) were not needed for the two in-scope assertions.

notes: Round 3 re-tested only the two assertions the orchestrator named after gcc-ut-fix-round2 (commit d8b41f4e): VAL-CROSS-007 end to end including the Sites chips after a warmed-cache reload, and the ETag clause of VAL-ONLINE-002. Result: both pass. Two flow-validator groups ran in two serial batches (A: r3-etag-api on curl, 2026-11-29; B: r3-cross007 on agent-browser App + Sites + curl, 2026-12-03) because r3-cross007's pacing/service-availability writes bump every bookable date's day version and would have invalidated batch A's cached ETag mid-test. The round-2 root cause is fixed: the first write on a never-mutated date now moves the public ETag (0 -> 1, and the Sites page serves the closed state on a plain reload), and a warmed client replaying the pre-change ETag gets 200 with the new body instead of 304 with the stale one. The second half of the fix also holds: operator availability now flags a max_parties-only breach (available:false, pacingWarning:true) and the staff booking path refuses with 409 pacing_parties_exceeded (201 + warnings + toast on the explicit override). All 181 assertions in this milestone's features' fulfills mapping are now passed in validation-state.json; VAL-CROSS-007's stale round-2 issue record was cleared. Environment: services stopped at the end of the round; group fixtures restored and parent-verified (0 special days >= 2026-12-01, 6 service-availability rows, 4 pacing rules, 2026-12-03 back to 28 slots).
